pairs.question: Siquid habent veri, visa quid ista ferant?
pairs.answer: Quem tu mobilibus foliis vitare volebas, sed male vitabas, aestus amoris erat.
pairs.derivation: After recounting his dream, the poet asks the dream-interpreter to explain it. Dropped the speech-framing/address 'Dic age, nocturnae, quicumque es, imaginis augur' (line 297), which narrates the asking and addresses the augur; kept the interrogative utterance 'siquid habent veri, visa quid ista ferant' (line 298), capitalized first word and put a ?. Answer: dropped the narration frame 'Sic ego; nocturnae sic dixit imaginis augur, expendens animo singula dicta suo:' (299-300); the augur's reply answers from its first word, so kept the first sentence (to the first full stop, lines 301-302), which interprets the dream's central image (the heat = the heat of love). What follows the cut is further interpretation of the other dream-symbols (vacca = puella, cornix = lena, etc., lines 303-310).
